# Next observation: CRA compressed-reference bytes after completion

**AI disclosure:** Generated by AI. Design only. This ticket does **not** authorize a hardware run or shipped patch.

## Question

Commands and copied controls already match across VA/Gst and pinned C (#71). Do compressed-reference **bytes** (four `fill_comp` regions plus MV) match for CRA picture 28 / POC32 and its first-bad consumers (Gst 29/POC28, VA 31/POC31)? Equal commands do not prove firmware guilt; differing compressed bytes after a completed write would be a content/lifetime observation, not by itself a firmware proof.

## Where and when

Userspace, after `DQBUF` of the capture buffer (process context, not IRQ/spinlock). The plane is then owned by userspace. Copy only:

- compressed window `[comp_start, comp_start+comp_size)` (177152 bytes)
- MV window `[length-mv_size, length)` (7168 bytes)

for pictures 28, 29, 31 of RPS_E VA and Gst, plus one RPS_B control picture. Do not hash the full 368128-byte VA pad. Do not walk buffers from `avd_irq`.

Identity: same-run writer generation, POC, allocation index, `memory` (MMAP vs DMABUF), `length`, `comp_*`, `mv_*` already in the reference snapshot. Bind copies to those records.

## Safety

CPU observation of a dequeued vb2 buffer does not require a kernel map in IRQ. Do not `dma_sync` from an experimental IRQ hook; that would be a coherency disturbance. If a future kernel dump is proposed, it needs its own reviewed default-off recorder, `dma_sync_for_cpu` only after job completion and outside spinlocks, finite size, and an off/on pixel-preservation campaign. This leaf does not implement that.

If even userspace copies cannot be shown not to affect later reuse, treat that as a blocked design and keep #42 open.

## Distinguishing

1. Compressed/MV bytes differ VA vs Gst for picture 28 while commands matched → client buffer packing/lifetime (length/MV placement), not a command bug.
2. Bytes match across clients, RPS_E still wrong → contents of these ranges are not the observed divergence; next is firmware-internal / cache not visible in the plane.
3. Bytes change between completion and first-bad consumer reuse of the same allocation → reuse/stale-content hypothesis, still not firmware-by-elimination.

Parent [driver #42](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/42) keeps the correction. No support-count change.
